Check a JWT and return its claims

Source: R/jwt.R
jose_jwt_decode.Rd

jose_jwt_decode() verifies a JWT's signature with jose_verify()'s rules and then checks its claims (RFC 7519, RFC 8725). The checks happen here, in one call, so none can be forgotten.

Usage

jose_jwt_decode(
  token,
  key,
  algorithms,
  audience = NULL,
  issuer = NULL,
  subject = NULL,
  type = "JWT",
  required = "exp",
  claims = list(),
  validate = NULL,
  max_age = NULL,
  leeway = 60,
  now = Sys.time(),
  decrypt = NULL,
  limits = jose_limits()
)

Arguments

token

The JWT, in the compact serialization.

key

A jose_key, a jose_keyset, or a function of the header returning one.

algorithms

The signature algorithms to accept, such as "HS256".

audience

The audiences this caller accepts, or NULL.

issuer

The issuer this caller accepts, or NULL.

subject

The subject this caller accepts, or NULL.

type

The expected typ, or NULL to skip the check.

required

Names of claims that must be present.

claims

Further expectations, as a named list of values or functions.

validate

A function of the claims list that must return TRUE, or NULL.

max_age

The greatest age, in seconds, of iat, or NULL.

leeway

Seconds of clock skew to allow.

now

The current time, as POSIXct.

decrypt

For a JWT sent as a JWE, the key and algorithms to decrypt it, from jose_decryption(); NULL refuses a JWE.

limits

Resource limits, from jose_limits().

Value

The claims, as a named list of class jose_claims, with exp, nbf and iat as POSIXct and the verified header as the header attribute.

Details

  • exp, nbf and iat must be numbers. The token must not have expired, must already be valid, and must not be issued in the future, each allowing leeway seconds. max_age bounds how long ago iat was.

  • required names claims that must be present. The default requires exp: a token that never expires has to be accepted on purpose.

  • issuer and subject must equal iss and sub exactly. An iss or sub that is not a single string is refused.

  • aud must contain one of audience. A token that names an audience is refused when audience is NULL (RFC 7519 section 4.1.3), and one without aud is refused when audience is given.

  • type must match the typ header, ignoring case and an application/ prefix. A token without typ passes only when type is "JWT".

  • claims holds further expectations, one per claim: a value the claim must equal, or a function of the claim that must return TRUE. validate is a function of the whole claims list, for checks across claims.

A JWT whose header has cty: "JWT" carries another JWT as its payload. That inner JWT is verified with the same key and algorithms, and its claims are checked. Deeper nesting is refused.

A JWT sent as a JWE is accepted only when decrypt says how to decrypt it, so a check meant for signed tokens never silently accepts encrypted ones. The JWE either carries a signed JWT (cty: "JWT"), verified as above, or the claims themselves.

Each failed check raises a subclass of zujwt_claim_error carrying the claim name: zujwt_expired_error, zujwt_not_yet_valid_error, zujwt_audience_error, zujwt_issuer_error, zujwt_subject_error or zujwt_missing_claim_error. Time errors also carry time and now.

See also

jose_jwt_decoder() to fix these arguments once.

Examples

key <- jose_key_oct(as.raw(1:32))
jwt <- jose_jwt_encode(list(iss = "me", aud = "api"), key, "HS256",
                       expires_in = 60)
claims <- jose_jwt_decode(jwt, key, "HS256", audience = "api",
                          issuer = "me")
claims$iss
#> [1] "me"

# Claim failures have classes of their own.
tryCatch(
  jose_jwt_decode(jwt, key, "HS256", audience = "other"),
  zujwt_audience_error = function(e) "wrong audience"
)
#> [1] "wrong audience"
